segment.description: Gulf Fork Big Creek — a small TWRA hatchery-supported trout tributary of the Big Creek drainage near the North Carolina line in Cocke County (catalog; HUC 06010105 French Broad, GNIS 01269381/01328352). Identity verified by county: TWRA's 2026 schedule carries 'Gulf Fork Big Creek' only under Cocke County; the Hawkins County 'Big Creek' rows in the same schedule are a different water, as is 'Trail Fork Big Creek' (sibling tributary).
segment.boundaries: Whole creek in Cocke County as stocked by TWRA; no formal agency reach boundaries. Two TDEC monitoring stations bracket the stream: TNW000002599 (35.9013, -83.0459, upper creek toward the NC-line headwaters) and TNW000002600 (35.8206, -83.0858, lower creek), both HUC 06010105.

coldSource.notes: No dam; no spring-fed characterization on record. Cool-water signal is observational, not structural: TDEC monitoring shows June-September surface water of 17.5-21.7 C at both the upper and lower stations (2020-2025), and the TWRA Trout Management Plan documents reproducing native Brook Trout in the stream's tributaries — a habitat that stays trout-viable through summer.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover record found; TWRA's program rows for the creek are five Seasonal-type (spring) Rainbow Trout stockings (weeks of 2/22 through 5/17/2026). However, the Trout Management Plan documents a naturally reproducing native Brook Trout population in the stream's tributaries (see wildPopulation), which is itself evidence of year-round survival in the headwater portion.

wildPopulation.detail: Reach caveat: the documented wild trout are in the TRIBUTARIES, not necessarily the stocked main reach. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 twice identifies 'Gulf Fork of Big Creek tributaries (Middle Prong Gulf Creek or Brown Gap Creek)' as a donor source of native Brook Trout for planned restoration projects (Table 1: 'Use fish from Gulf Fork tribs'; Little Paint Creek rationale), which documents a self-sustaining native Brook Trout population in this stream system's headwater tributaries.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC monitoring at two stations bracketing the creek shows June-September water of 17.5-21.7 C (2020-2025) and the TWRA Trout Management Plan documents reproducing native Brook Trout in Gulf Fork of Big Creek's tributaries — a stream system that demonstrably holds trout through summer, though the brook evidence is tributary-level and the main stocked reach is stocked as spring-only put-and-take.
